dossier_meta.authors: Araújo, Julio, Cohen, Nathann, Giroire, Frédéric, Havet, Frédéric
dossier_meta.subject: Graph Theory » Coloring » Labeling
dossier_meta.statement_text: Question What is the maximum edge density of a graph which has a good edge labeling? We say that a graph is good-edge-labeling critical , if it has no good edge labeling, but every proper subgraph has a good edge labeling. Conjecture For every $ c<4 $ , there is only a finite number of good-edge-labeling critical graphs with average degree less than $ c $ .
dossier_meta.context_text: Let $ G $ be a finite undirected simple graph. A good edge labeling of $ G $ is an assignment of distinct numbers to the edges such that every cycle has at least two local maxima. (The distinctness of the labels is required only to make the term `local maximum' unambiguous.) Equivalently, a labeling of the edges is good, if for every pair of distinct vertices $ u,v $ , there is at most one increasing path from $ u $ to $ v $ . Having a good edge labeling is inherited by subgraphs. It is easy to verify that the graphs $ K_3 $ and $ K_{2,3} $ have no good edge labeling. In [ACGH2] an infinite class of graphs without good edge labelings is given, none of whom is a subgraph of the other. In [BFT] contains an example of a minimal graph without good edge labeling which as average degree < 3 (thus refuting an earlier conjecture saying that a good-edge-labeling critical graph with average degree less than three is either $ K_3 $ or $ K_{2,3} $ ). In that same paper it is shown that every such graph must have girth at most 4. Good edge labeling of graphs was introduced in [BCP] in the context of the so-called Routing and Wavelength Assignment (RWA) problem. The problems above are proposed in [ACGH1] and [ACGH2]. There the algorithmic problem of determining whether a graph has a good edge labeling is shown to be NP-hard. Moreover, the authors also prove that every planar graph with girth at least six has a good edge labeling.
